phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem. In this problem,
a person is standing at a certain distance from a tower.
The angle of elevation of the top of the tower is
thirty degrees.
Then the person walks twenty meters towards the tower.
Now the angle becomes forty-five degrees,
and we need to find the height of the tower.
Let the distance from the tower after walking be x,
so the initial distance becomes x plus twenty.
Let the height of the tower be
h.
Now,
let us start with the second position where the angle is forty-five degrees.
Here we know the opposite side and the adjacent side.
So tan theta is the right trigonometric ratio to use.
Tan theta is equal to height by base.
Tan forty-five degrees is equal to h by
x.
We know tan forty-five degrees is one, so h by x is equal to one,
which means
h is equal to
x.
Got it?
Perfect. Now keep this value with us.
We will use it in the next step.
Now let us use the first position where the angle is thirty degrees. Again, we will use tan theta.
Tan thirty degree is equal to h by x plus twenty. We know tan thirty degree is one by root three.
So one by root three is equal to h by x plus twenty.
Since we already know h is equal to x, we replace x with h.
This becomes one by root three is equal to h by
h plus twenty. Cross-multiplying h plus twenty is equal to root three h.
So twenty is equal to
h into root three minus one. Therefore, h is equal to twenty by root three minus one. Now rationalize the denominator.
We get h is equal to ten into root three plus one. Done and dusted. So the final answer will be ten into root three plus one meter. Hence, option B is correct.
